name: composer-list-closing

escalations.question: Should the Composer's slash-command list close when the textarea loses focus (backlog row from 20261112-2120, `const listOpen` in src/renderer/src/composer/Composer.tsx)?
escalations.answer: Yes: close the list on blur (answered in prose at Gate 1 with the track confirmation).

escalations.question: While the slash-command list is open, should Esc only close the list (as signed by 20261112-2120) or close it and also interrupt the running turn (`handleListKey` in src/renderer/src/composer/Composer.tsx)?
escalations.answer: Keep close-only, as signed (answered in prose at Gate 1).

criteria: C1: With the list open, blurring the Composer textarea closes the list (no listbox rendered, `aria-expanded` not true); a test drives the blur and asserts it.
C2: After a blur-close, focusing the textarea again with a draft that still matches reopens the list; a test asserts it.

C3: Clicking a row (mousedown on the row, as `SlashCommandList.tsx` handles it) still accepts it and writes `/<name> ` to the draft; the existing row-click test still passes, and the blur rule does not break it.

C4: A dismissal made by Esc is cleared whenever the draft differs from the dismissed text, by whatever route it changed: a test dismisses with Esc, rerenders with a different `state.text` from the parent, then rerenders back to the dismissed text with no local edit, and asserts the list is open.
C5: Esc with the list open still only closes the list and does not call `onInterrupt` (behaviour unchanged, E2); an Esc with the list closed still interrupts. Existing tests for both stay green.
C6: The `dismissedFor` docblock and the `handleListKey` comment in `Composer.tsx` describe the new rules accurately, with no session ids or `.sir/` paths in source.
C7: `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass in the repository root; each new test fails when its rule is reverted (red step).
